results.title: Ukraine seeks €115 billion in foreign aid for 2027, Zelensky says
results.content: Ukraine will need €115 billion in external financing next year to sustain its economy and war effort against Russia, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday, adding that Kyiv had secured commitments for about €90 billion from the European Union.

results.title: New York jury convicts Huawei of stealing trade secrets
results.content: A New York jury has found Chinese telecom giant Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets and other criminal offences, but acquitted it of a racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice. The verdict followed a three-month trial in New York in a case that adds to longstanding US efforts to curb Huawei's operations over alleged threats to national security.

results.title: Champions League: Real Madrid thrash PSV 5-1 in comeback win as Manchester City held by Napoli
results.content: Real Madrid extended their winning run to 10 games in all competitions on Tuesday, overturning an early deficit to rout PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League, with Jude Bellingham scoring a spectacular goal and Kylian Mbappé netting twice. Manchester City, meanwhile, twice came from behind to draw 2-2 with Napoli, while Arsenal were held to a 1-1 draw by Borussia Dortmund.

results.title: Tech executives' investment in Trump 'clearly paying off' as Huang reinstated at Nvidia
results.content: Nvidia shares fell on Tuesday as the historic rally sparked by Jensen Huang's return as CEO quickly lost steam, with investors refocusing ​on the political ‌and governance risks surrounding his reinstatement. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, The Hill Senior Technology Reporter Miranda Nazzaro says that the reinstatement of Jensen Huang at Nvidia represents "the culmination of a two-year push of tech executives to get closer to President Trump and their investment in the President is clearly paying off".

results.title: Tech executives' investment in Trump 'clearly paying off' as Huang reinstated at Nvidia
results.content: Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, The Hill Senior Technology Reporter Miranda Nazzaro says that the reinstatement of Jensen Huang at Nvidia represents "the culmination of a two-year push of tech executives to get closer to President Trump and their investment in the President is clearly paying off".

results.title: 'Quid pro quo’: Nvidia too big to fail or ‘too close to personal interest of people around Trump’?
results.content: Angela Diffley is pleased to welcome Bernard Benhamou, Secretary General of the Institute of Digital Sovereignty and Senior Lecturer in Internet Governance at Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne University. What does Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia mean for Trump, Lutnick, the US, the AI industry and China? Describing Huang as “the global banker of the AI industry”, Benhamou explains: “He is the visionary, he is the banker. He's not only the chip maker.” He also warns of the repercussions of Donald Trump's decision to reinstate the Nvidia CEO, with congressional and judicial scrutiny looming. “It's far from over. It's just the beginning.”

results.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia comeback sends AI videos into overdrive
results.content: Just 11 days after resigning as Nvidia CEO, Jensen Huang’s return has unleashed a fresh wave of AI-generated videos. But the internet has changed its tune: while last week’s memes mocked Huang, many now celebrate his comeback. One viral video purportedly showing him dancing is actually AI-manipulated footage of a basketball coach from 2016. From humiliation to hero worship, the technology Nvidia helped popularise is rewriting the narrative surrounding its own CEO, as Vedika Bahl explains.

results.title: Did Nvidia knowingly send chips to China 'cutout'? Was there ‘pay-to-play’ involving Trump, Lutnick?
results.content: François Picard is pleased to welcome Andrew Weissmann, Professor of Practice at NYU School of Law and a former federal prosecutor known for leading major Department of Justice (DOJ) and FBI investigations. “Why were they treating Nvidia so favorably? Professor Weissmann joins us to discuss the legal and ethical questions surrounding the Trump administration's dealings with the chipmaker. He examines allegations of personal financial gain, the implications for US national security, the limits of presidential immunity and what he describes as an “unholy alliance of tech bros, of Wall Street, and of politicians."

results.title: Senegal reinstated as AFCON 2025 winners
results.content: In tonight's edition, Senegal were reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners after the sport's highest court upheld their appeal against being stripped of the title.

results.title: UN slams Iran after it flogs singer for performing without veil
results.content: The United Nations condemned as "abhorrent" the flogging of Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her production team, urging Tehran to abolish the practice. The five received 74 lashes each on Monday following a performance viewed millions of times on YouTube, local media reported, citing Ahmadi's lawyer.

results.title: Russian nuclear satellites plan 'foolhardy', expert says
results.content: NATO chief Mark Rutte said Monday the alliance would defend against threats in space when asked about German media reports that Russia may be preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Jennie Shin, Dafydd Townley, Senior Teaching Fellow in International Security at the University of Portsmouth, says that the alleged plan would be "foolhardy because the impact would be indiscriminate, they wouldn't be able to choose only Western or non-Russian satellites".

results.title: The Bukele method: will Salvadoran leader's strong-arm tactics work for Haiti?
results.content: Haitians are hailing the Bukele method. Citizens of the Americas’ poorest nation cheering the Salvadoran president’s ’shoot first, ask questions later’ method of dealing with the gangs that have overrun their country the past six years. Can the police force deployed actually restore law and order? We’ll ask about the latest in a decades-long list of efforts by the international community to support Haiti.

results.title: Senegal AFCON ruling 'good in the books of sports law', expert says
results.content: Speaking with FRANCE 24's Jennie Shin, sports presenter and journalist Thando Sibiya explains that the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport to reinstate Senegal as ⁠winner of ​the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations "from a jurisprudence perspective or creating precedent, it is going to be good in the books of sports law, because if every single decision of a referee is taken to a court of law all the time, it really tampers with the quality, governance and legitimacy of the game".

results.title: Senegal regain AFCON title on appeal at Morocco's expense
results.content: Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January. CAS said in a statement it had "upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF)" by a "unanimous decision". FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

results.title: Car bomb destroys buildings in central Colombian city
results.content: A car bomb detonated in the central Colombian city of Villavicencio on Monday, destroying a local governor's office and surrounding buildings, President Abelardo de la Espriella said. The right-wing leader has conducted a major crackdown on the country's drug trade, in response to left-wing FARC rebels who have stepped up attacks over the past two years. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington reports.

results.title: Russian losses on Ukrainian front top 700,000 including missing
results.content: New analysis of leaked Russian government data suggests more than 700,000 Russian soldiers have died in the war against Ukraine. Independent Russian media outlets have updated their estimates of Moscow's military casualties, including soldiers missing on the frontline, after Belarusian and Ukrainian hackers obtained figures from the Russian statistics agency. FRANCE 24's Carys Garland explains.

results.title: Gunmen hold 30 people hostage at supermarket in Colombia's Cartagena
results.content: Armed robbers took some 30 people hostage at a supermarket in Colombia’s tourist city of Cartagena on Tuesday, prompting a major police operation and a temporary suspension of incoming flights, authorities said. Landings at Rafael Nunez International Airport resumed after the military used a runway during the operation.

results.title: Russia's war on Ukraine: 'Both sides are prepared to operate outside of the conflict zone'
results.content: Charli James is pleased to welcome Gavin Hall, Teaching Fellow in Political Science, and International Security at the University of Strathclyde. Hall examines recent Russian and Ukrainian operations beyond the main conflict zone, the conditions necessary for a negotiated settlement and the implications of diminishing direct US military support for Ukraine. “Both sides are prepared to operate beyond the main battleground and outside of the conflict zone,” he explains. Hall discusses why both sides want to negotiate from a position of strength and the conditions under which a “mutually hurting stalemate” could lead to a negotiated settlement.

results.title: Yemen’s army says Houthi fighters closing in on government stronghold of Aden
results.content: Yemen's military on Tuesday said that Houthi fighters were closing in on the internationally recognised government's stronghold of Aden from about 60km (40 miles) away and vowed to repel any assault. A military spokesman said defences were prepared following Houthi advances and government pullbacks near the Red Sea.

results.title: France's ex-president Nicolas Sarkozy, wife Carla Bruni to stand trial for alleged witness tampering
results.content: France's former president Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife, singer Carla Bruni-Sarkozy, are set to be tried in 2027 on charges of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" as well as benefitting from witness tampering. The new charges are related to the Sarkozy couple's actions during the case examining illegal campaign funding from Libyan strongman Muammar Gaddafi over which Sarkozy was imprisoned last year.

results.title: 'We are ready to facilitate removal of Netanyahu': Head of Israel's Arab-majority Joint List
results.content: In an interview with FRANCE 24, the head of the Arab-majority Joint List said his political alliance is prepared to play a decisive role in bringing down Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government following the recent election. "We are ready to facilitate the removal of Netanyahu" from power, Yousef Jabareen said, signalling a willingness to explore political alliances beyond traditional divisions in Israeli politics.

results.title: Senegal reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners
results.content: Senegal ​were reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners ​on Tuesday after the Court of Arbitration for Sport upheld their appeal against being stripped of the title. Senegal contested the ​Confederation ‌of African Football's decision to declare ⁠Morocco champions, despite Senegal beating the hosts 1-0 after extra time in ‌January's final in Rabat. Morocco announced that it would “pursue all necessary legal procedures” in response to the decision.

results.title: 'Tis the season to be green: Can the Christmas holidays be a present for the planet?
results.content: With the holiday season just around the corner, we take a look at its environmental impact. We discuss how to make Christmas a little greener as consumers, whether plastic trees or natural ones are better for the planet, and what small steps we can all take to reduce our carbon footprint during the festivities.

results.title: French police officer who shot teenager to face murder trial
results.content: A French police officer will stand trial for murder in the killing of a teenager in 2023 that sparked violent protests across the country, the Versailles appeals court said on Tuesday. Nahel Merzouk, 17, was shot in the Paris suburb of Nanterre after he failed to comply with an order to stop his car.
